claim.quote: Here, we show that a silicon crystal glued to its holder exhibits a rate of low-energy phonon events that is more than two orders of magnitude larger than in a functionally identical crystal suspended from its holder in a low-stress state.

name: A Stress Induced Source of Phonon Bursts and Quasiparticle Poisoning
notes: Listed on the TESSERACT papers page; the TAUP 2025 slides cite it under SPICE ('suppress a stress induced LEE source from the holder'). The arXiv paper itself carries no collaboration tag.

summary.plain: Gluing a silicon crystal to its holder produced hundreds of times more tiny vibration bursts than suspending the same kind of crystal with little stress. The bursts fade after cooldown, which points to stress as one cause of the low-energy excess that hampers dark matter detectors.
summary.technical: Comparison of a glued and a suspended silicon crystal: the excess phonon event rate in the glued crystal decreases with time since cooldown, consistent with relaxation of thermally induced stress between glue and crystal; relevant to quasiparticle poisoning in qubits and to the low-energy events of cryogenic calorimeters.

title: A Stress Induced Source of Phonon Bursts and Quasiparticle Poisoning
why_it_matters: The abstract ties the stress mechanism to low-energy events seen in cryogenic calorimeters, one of the main limiting backgrounds for sub-GeV dark matter searches.
